title: Playing with Buddy Petit and his illness
summary: Tillman played jitney dances and country work with Buddy Petit, who was weak and sick; he blames exposure and hard drinking for early deaths among musicians.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Joe Yeah that was a Jitney.

Well I played with Buddy there. I had been playing in the band. We had been getting a whole lot of work over the lake around Madisonville and Maddenville all over there. He came from over there around Maddenville. Somewhere over there. And he was well known. People liked him you know. And I was playing with the band. Well at that time he had kind of lost his health. He got so sick and weak I would say that I was mostly holding him up letting him you know try to make a piece of bread because I was playing sax. And he had got so weak he couldn't hardly hit off sometimes. He used to make me hit the band off for him. We played up there a while and things like start to go in bed around there and the guy played us a week and ran off with the money and didn't pay off. Well then Buddy got out and so sick then he couldn't play no more and recently after that he died.
What was he sick of? Was there any particular sickness that he had?

Well I wouldn't know exactly but Buddy had so much exposure I mad about running the TV. That's what it looked more like because I never did hear what he died with but that's what he looked more like. He used to drink hard and plenty night exposure, play them dances and go out in the air and all like that. That's where the most of the old musicians died from exposure to help kill itself you know. He get in them hot places and come out with no coats on. A man can track a whole lot of coal like that. It'd feel good to him right then but up in the ages you begin feeling it. And I think that was mostly his trouble. I played with old man Gus Metcalf, Noel Foster. We used to have practice all our work over the lake too around Beter Spring. All the white places, most of the big white places that was giving dances, outings. We used to play over there. I played with Kid Thomas band. I made more money with his band than the band I ever made it with. Yeah?
